quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "rose" slowly and isolate just the target consonant. To make /z/, you push a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with your voice on. To make /s/, you push a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice. Which one are you actually doing?
quests.explanation: "rose" features /z/ rather than /s/. /z/ comes from pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with your voice on, which is why it sounds distinct from the voiceless alveolar fricative /s/ used in words like "see".
quests.mouthPosition: Push a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with your voice on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: In "shed", focus on the target sound. /ʃ/ comes from rounding your lips slightly and pushing air across your tongue with no voice, while /tʃ/ comes from stopping the air just behind your top teeth, then releasing it as a hiss, with no voice — which one is really happening?
quests.explanation: In "shed", the target sound is /ʃ/, made by rounding your lips slightly and pushing air across your tongue with no voice. The distractor /tʃ/ would instead require you to stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with no voice — a clearly different sound once you isolate it.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, round your lips slightly and push air across your tongue with no voice.
